\section{Theorems}

\begin{theorem}[Main]
For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $\delta > 0$ such that $|x| < \delta$
implies $|f(x)| < \varepsilon$.
\label{thm:main}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}
The set $A$ is closed and bounded.
\label{prop:one}
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}
If $A$ is compact then $f(A)$ is compact.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}
A map $f$ is continuous at $x_{0}$ if $\lim_{x \to x_{0}} f(x) = f(x_{0})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proof}
Take $\delta = \varepsilon/2$. Then by Theorem~\ref{thm:main} the claim
follows, and Proposition~\ref{prop:one} gives boundedness.
\end{proof}
